meta.method: Bottom-up clustering of 524 free-form problem tags from 275 people (75 founders + 200 non-founders)

clusters.name: Children not being seen
clusters.tagline: Children dismissed, labelled, hit, or left to face the worst alone
clusters.turnsInto: Child development consulting, play therapy, progressive education, parenting coaching, youth advocacy, family support services
clusters.essence: The underlying brokenness is: adults treating children as less than whole people, whether through neglect, control, labels, or violence
representativeTags: children being treated as less than whole people
adults imposing their pace on children instead of watching
children labelled uneducable by institutions that never tried
children facing the darkest moments of history alone
adults remembering children as cartoons instead of people
children not learning because nobody in the building likes them
teachers blaming students for not learning instead of examining their own teaching
traumatised children being fixed instead of understood

placemakes.label: Children being treated as less than whole people
placemakes.example: Like Fred Rogers airing a full minute of silence on television because he believed children deserved time to think about who loved them

placemakes.label: Children labelled uneducable by institutions that never tried
placemakes.example: Like Maria Montessori taking children from asylums labelled uneducable, designing tactile materials, and watching them pass standard Italian public school exams

placemakes.label: Children facing the darkest moments of history alone
placemakes.example: Like Janusz Korczak refusing offers to escape the Warsaw Ghetto, reportedly saying 'You do not leave children at a time like this,' then walking with 192 orphans to the Umschlagplatz

placemakes.label: Children not learning because nobody in the building likes them
placemakes.example: Like Rita Pierson grounding her whole case on James Comer's line: 'No significant learning can occur without a significant relationship'

placemakes.label: Traumatised children being fixed instead of understood
placemakes.example: Like Dan Hughes coining the PACE stance and saying 'If you're not curious, you're fixing. And traumatised children know when they are being fixed'

clusters.name: Voices being silenced
clusters.tagline: People whose voice was taken, suppressed, punished, or never allowed to exist
clusters.turnsInto: Advocacy, voice coaching, expressive arts therapy, storytelling workshops, media platforms, memoir facilitation, protest art
clusters.essence: The underlying brokenness is: people being prevented from saying what they see, feel, or know, whether by governments, institutions, culture, or trauma
representativeTags: childhood trauma stealing a person's voice
women being punished for speaking about what is done to them
military dictatorships silencing artists who give people a voice
citizens being forced to perform lies they no longer believe
Black talent being rejected by institutions that claim to value merit
speaking truth to power costing you your country
women's voices being silenced in public life for thousands of years
governments silencing journalists who expose the truth

placemakes.label: Childhood trauma stealing a person's voice
placemakes.example: Like Maya Angelou going mute for nearly five years at age eight after being raped, until a family friend coaxed her out of silence by asking her to read poetry aloud

placemakes.label: Military dictatorships silencing artists who give people a voice
placemakes.example: Like Mercedes Sosa being arrested on stage mid-performance in 1979, along with her entire audience, then forced into exile for three years

placemakes.label: Truth-tellers being murdered to maintain silence
placemakes.example: Like Anna Politkovskaya warning 'People sometimes pay with their lives for saying aloud what they think,' then being shot dead in her elevator ten months later

placemakes.label: Women's voices being silenced in public life for thousands of years
placemakes.example: Like Mary Beard tracing silencing from Homer's Odyssey to Hillary Clinton, quoting Telemachus telling his mother to go and weave: 'That line is 2,800 years old and it still works in 2017'

placemakes.label: Speaking truth to power costing you your country
placemakes.example: Like Miriam Makeba testifying at the UN asking for an arms embargo on South Africa, then having her citizenship revoked, leaving her stateless for nearly 30 years

clusters.name: Bodies in pain
clusters.tagline: Physical suffering that nobody names, treats, or takes seriously enough
clusters.turnsInto: Health coaching, chronic illness support, pain management, somatic therapy, end-of-life care, sleep consulting, body-based healing practices
clusters.essence: The underlying brokenness is: bodies in pain being ignored, undertreated, or separated from the person inside them
representativeTags: a body in constant pain with no way to express what that feels like
people dying in pain because hospitals weren't designed for dying
society treating sleep deprivation as a badge of honour
people dying in surgery from errors a simple checklist could prevent
poor people dying of treatable diseases because the system decided they weren't worth treating
patients being reduced to diagnoses instead of seen as whole people
illness being loaded with shame through metaphors like battle and invasion
burnout being glorified as the price of success

placemakes.label: A body in constant pain with no way to express what that feels like
placemakes.example: Like Frida Kahlo, whose bus accident at 18 broke her spine in three places and her right leg in eleven, painting from a mirror above her hospital bed for the rest of her life

placemakes.label: People dying in pain because hospitals were not designed for dying
placemakes.example: Like Cicely Saunders introducing the concept of total pain, arguing that opioid dosing had to be anticipatory rather than waiting for the patient to beg, then dying in her own hospice using the protocols she designed

placemakes.label: Poor people dying of treatable diseases because the system decided they were not worth treating
placemakes.example: Like Paul Farmer walking eight hours to reach one patient because he argued the rural poor deserved the same treatment standards as patients at Harvard hospitals

placemakes.label: Society treating sleep deprivation as a badge of honour
placemakes.example: Like Matthew Walker showing that even a one-hour sleep loss from daylight saving causes measurable spikes in heart attacks

placemakes.label: Burnout being glorified as the price of success
placemakes.example: Like Arianna Huffington collapsing from exhaustion and breaking her cheekbone on her desk, then spending years building Thrive Global to change how the world thinks about burnout

clusters.name: The planet breaking
clusters.tagline: Ecological destruction, species loss, and climate crisis happening while most people look away
clusters.turnsInto: Environmental consulting, sustainability coaching, regenerative design, climate communication, conservation education, eco-business strategy
clusters.essence: The underlying brokenness is: humans destroying the living systems they depend on, and not enough people noticing or acting
representativeTags: ecological collapse happening while most people don't notice
industrial chemicals poisoning the natural world while governments look away
species being wiped out without anyone noticing or caring
the climate crisis being treated as a future problem instead of a present emergency
business growth destroying the natural world it depends on

exponential growth on a finite planet being treated as normal
humans managing land without understanding they are part of it

placemakes.label: Industrial chemicals poisoning the natural world while governments look away
placemakes.example: Like Rachel Carson publishing Silent Spring while dying of cancer she kept secret, exposing DDT bioaccumulation the chemical industry had been hiding since the 1940s

placemakes.label: The climate crisis being treated as a future problem instead of a present emergency
placemakes.example: Like Greta Thunberg saying 'I don't want you to be hopeful. I want you to panic. I want you to feel the fear I feel every day. And then I want you to act'

placemakes.label: Western language making it impossible to treat the natural world as alive
placemakes.example: Like Robin Wall Kimmerer noting that in Potawatomi 'to be a bay' is a verb, while in English 'we'd never call our grandmother it, yet we do so with every plant, tree, and river we meet'

placemakes.label: Business growth destroying the natural world it depends on
placemakes.example: Like Yvon Chouinard transferring ownership of Patagonia to fight the climate crisis, saying 'Earth is now our only shareholder'

clusters.name: Power crushing people

an entire population being dehumanized by law based on skin colour

an entire nation being ruled by a foreign power through everyday compliance

placemakes.label: People being owned as property
placemakes.example: Like Harriet Tubman escaping slavery and returning to the South roughly 13 times to guide approximately 70 enslaved people to freedom, with no record of her ever losing a passenger

placemakes.label: An entire population being dehumanized by law based on skin colour
placemakes.example: Like Desmond Tutu spending decades confronting apartheid, from writing warnings to the Prime Minister to chairing the Truth and Reconciliation Commission

placemakes.label: Citizens being forced to perform lies they no longer believe

placemakes.label: Ordinary people having no power against institutions that control their lives
placemakes.example: Like Saul Alinsky building the modern template for community organising rooted in institutions people already belonged to, like parishes and unions, not abstract movements

placemakes.label: Democracies collapsing because citizens obey in advance without being asked
placemakes.example: Like Timothy Snyder noting 'Most of the power of authoritarianism is freely given. The Nazis did not have to demand compliance from most institutions. The institutions offered it'

overlapFlags.note: Significant overlap. Many tags about state censorship and political silencing could belong in either cluster. Decision rule: if the core brokenness is about having no voice, it goes in 'voices_silenced'. If it is about being dominated or controlled by power, it goes in 'power_crushing'. Tags about activists who were silenced BY power structures are placed in 'power_crushing' when the activism was the point, and 'voices_silenced' when the silencing was the point.

Creative silencing overlaps with general silencing. Decision rule: if the person is primarily an artist and the brokenness is about art being dismissed or constrained, it goes in 'creative_dismissed'. If the silencing is political or identity-based, it goes in 'voices_silenced'.

Identity erasure often comes with silencing. Decision rule: if the core brokenness is about WHO someone is allowed to be, it goes in 'identity_stolen'. If it is about WHAT someone is allowed to say, it goes in 'voices_silenced'.

Some education tags (Escalante, Gruwell, Kohl) could go in either cluster. Decision rule: if the problem is about children specifically being dismissed or mistreated, it goes in 'children_unseen'. If the problem is about knowledge or education being inaccessible generally, it goes in 'knowledge_locked'.
Burnout tags (Huffington) bridge both clusters. Placed primarily in 'work_without_soul' since burnout is work-caused, with body-specific health tags in 'bodies_suffering'.

gapFlags.description: Design and craft: tags about good design, thoughtful making, and the relationship between form and use. These are currently split between 'creative_dismissed', 'systems_not_caring', and 'knowledge_locked'. Could become its own cluster ('Things made badly') but the tags are too few and diverse (gardens, furniture, typography, buildings) to hold together as one felt category.

Grief and loss: scattered tags about grief (Patti Smith, Rumi, Elaine Pagels, Akira Kurosawa) are currently in 'meaning_missing' but could be their own cluster if the dataset were larger. At 8-10 tags it does not reach critical mass.

Women specifically: a large cross-cutting theme of women being dismissed, silenced, exploited, and forced into roles appears across at least 8 clusters. Rather than pulling it out as a separate cluster (which would gut the others), it stays distributed. But a future version might add a 'women_pushed_aside' lens or tag.
